title: Access Certificates Retention Scheduler and Evidence Pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Compliance teams need deterministic, auditable evidence that user and service account access certificates (SSO sessions, SCIM-provisioned entitlements, privileged role changes) are retained according to customer/region residency and retention policies, and surfaced in a single reportable artifact. Current evidence is fragmented across logs, SCIM delta feeds, and ad-hoc export scripts.

This ticket implements a scheduler and pipeline that: 1) computes retention windows per-tenant based on residency and contract; 2) materializes snapshot artifacts (signed, chunked) for periodic access reviews; 3) retains a short-term fast path for on-demand queries and a long-term cold archive for regulatory exports; and 4) wires the artifacts into the automated evidence export system used by Report Runner and Audit Playbooks. The goal is to reduce manual evidence collection time from days to minutes and provide provable chain-of-custody metadata for auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler computes tenant retention windows using residency map and tiered retention config (per-tenant override supported)
Pipeline emits snapshot artifacts with schema v2 (header with residency, policy, signer, version) and per-file checksums
Artifacts are uploaded to customer-scoped secure bucket and indexed in the Evidence Catalog within 15 minutes of snapshot completion
On-demand evidence queries for a tenant within retention window return signed artifact URLs and a deterministic manifest
End-to-end integration tests and one customer staging run complete without leaking PII outside tenant region
tasks: Design retention config schema and integrate with residency service (Config: default/region/tenant)
Implement Scheduler service (cron + event-driven fallback) with rate-limiting and jitter to avoid burst load
Build Snapshotter that queries RBAC store, SCIM delta service, and SSO session exporter to produce canonical access certificate bundles
Add signer component (KMS-backed) to attach chain-of-custody metadata and checksum to each artifact
Integrate artifact uploads with Evidence Catalog (indexing metadata, lifecycle tags) and secure storage routing based on residency
Create automated test harness and compliance smoke tests (integration with staging tenant)
Document runbook and add observability: per-tenant metrics and alerting for missed snapshots
Coordinate with Legal and Security for key rotation and retention policy edge cases
notes: We will reuse parts of existing evidence exporter used by ENG-115231 where possible to avoid duplication
Retention defaults: 90 days for hosted, 180 days for enterprise standard, configurable per-contract via BPM
Signed artifacts will include a compact JSON header and gzipped newline-delimited JSON body to balance readability and size
Design decision: use eventual consistency for SCIM deltas during snapshot to avoid blocking long tails; provide a reconciliation job that tightens gaps
Keep a fast 'recent index' in DB for quick on-demand retrieval spanning the last 30 days; older artifacts go to cold archive
artifacts: Design spec doc: Doc v1.0 - Access Certificates Retention Scheduler (internal link)
Dashboards: GC Evidence Pipeline - Scheduler Metrics (Grafana)
decisions: Use KMS-backed asymmetric signing to enable cross-team verification without exposing private keys
Materialize per-tenant manifests rather than trying per-object queries at export time to simplify auditor workflows
Retention overrides are validated by Contract Service and fall back to default on validation failure
SCIM snapshot includes lastProcessedDeltaId to aid reconciliation and troubleshooting
roll_out_plan: Phase 1: Internal staging rollout on non-prod tenants (2 weeks) - validate correctness and performance
Phase 2: Pilot with 3 enterprise customers across NA/EU to validate residency routing and contracts (1 month)
Phase 3: General availability for self-serve tenants with UI toggle and audit logging (GA)
Feature flag control in console to enable/disable per-tenant snapshot scheduling
qa_plan: Unit tests for scheduler jitter, rate limits, and retention computation
Integration tests that spin up a staging tenant, create SCIM changes and SSO sessions, and verify snapshot artifacts
Load test: simulate 5k tenants with randomized retention windows to measure scheduling scale
Compliance verification: ensure artifacts include residency tags and signed checksum; validate KMS signing and verification flow
risks: Burst scheduling could overwhelm Snapshotter if many tenants align — mitigated by per-region token bucket and backoff
Incorrect retention mapping could violate contracts — require Contract Service validation and pre-deploy contract sanity checks
Signing key compromise risk — mitigated via KMS rotation policy and keyless verification path for auditors
Large artifacts may incur cross-region egress costs — pipeline routes uploads to tenant-region buckets where possible
monitoring: Alert: >0.5% failed snapshots across rolling 24h for any region
Dashboard: per-tenant retention compliance view and evidence catalog ingestion lag
Audit log: every snapshot run writes a signed run-record to the Audit Stream
